The *Samuṭṭhānasīsasaṅkhepa* ("The thirteen groups of originations of offenses") is the third chapter of the *Parivāra*, the final collection of the Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The text opens with an introductory sequence of verses regarding the Dhamma and systematically summarizes the monastic rules and their various points of origination (*samuṭṭhāna*) in metrical verse form [SuttaCentral]. Modern translations cataloged by SuttaCentral include an English rendering by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

While SuttaCentral does not record curated canonical parallels, text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus highlights extensive Pali-internal transmission, identifying 135 matching passages across nine texts [DharmaNexus]. The heaviest overlap occurs with post-canonical Vinaya manuals and commentaries, most prominently the *Vinayavinicchaya* (sharing over 3,300 characters, notably §51.3–56.4) and its subcommentary, the *Vinayavinicchayaṭīkā*, alongside the *Parivāra-aṭṭhakathā*, *Vimativinodanī-ṭīkā*, and *Sāratthadīpanī-ṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. The work also exhibits internal reuse within the *Parivāra* itself, sharing passages (§28.2–29.2) with the *Katthapaññattivāra* (Pvr 1.1) [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language machine alignments identified by DharmaNexus link portions of the text to Sanskrit Vinaya sources—such as the *Prātimokṣasūtra*, *Poṣadhavastu*, and *Saṅghabhedavastu*—and Tibetan canonical and commentarial Vinaya works including the *Bhikṣuvarṣāgrapṛcchā*, *Pratimokṣasūtrapaddhati*, and the *Vinayasūtra* [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
